name: floating-player
title: Floating player
description: Keeps a playing video in view: when it scrolls away it docks to a corner as a mini player that never restarts, with a close button.
docs: Wrap any player in it (a video element, an iframe or your own component) and tell it whether the media is playing with playing. While the player is on screen nothing changes. When it scrolls out of view during playback, the same element docks to a corner as a mini player (dock is bottom-right by default or bottom-left, width is a number of px or any CSS length, 320 by default, never wider than the screen minus 2rem): the child is not moved or re-created, only restyled with position fixed, so playback never restarts, and a placeholder of the same height, with a dashed outline and a short note, keeps the page from jumping and shows where it went. It counts as in view while about a fifth of it is on screen. A video that is not playing is never docked; once docked, pausing keeps the mini player so it can be resumed. The mini player is a labelled region ('Product tour, mini player', from label) with a Close button and a 'Back to video' link that scrolls to the placeholder; Escape closes it from inside it and from anywhere nothing else has focus (a menu or dialog that takes the key keeps it), and docking is announced once. Closing calls onClose, where you pause the media, and the player stays in its place until the video has been seen again; onDock(true | false) tells you when it docks and when it returns. Focus goes to the player when the mini player closes or you go back. It keeps clear of a phone's safe area (env(safe-area-inset-*), at least 1rem from each edge), and under reduced motion it docks without the slide. Do not put it inside an element with a transform, filter or contain: paint, which would make fixed mean fixed inside that element. The scroll can be the page's or any scroll container's. labels holds the words for another language. The rhs-float-in keyframes and its animate-rhs-float-in variable come with the item.
